title: E4.1: full-row transient check of the row model for the gain-stage cell set (check V1 of E4 repeated for GS)
question: Does the behavioural row model of E4 (bound violation, or per-instance leakage summed by inverse-time additivity) predict the match-line crossing time of rows built from the gain-stage cell set GS as well as it did for the 6T2M cell set in check V1?
why: Check V1 of E4 compared the row model with full-row transient SPICE only for the 6T2M cell set (arm xt). The gs arm of E4 uses the same rule with the LBUF chain (divider node X -> INV_S -> INV_S -> pull-down) for the lower bounds and the UINV chain for the upper bounds; no full-row simulation of these rows exists. The revised paper uses the gain-stage cell as the main system-level test of the node ranking.
status_of_e4: E4 and its decisions are not changed by this step; it adds a validation of one model input of the gs arm.

inputs.models: the sky130 subset of E4 (E4_config.json: models.lib); the mismatch draws of the E4 pools (pool_draws of E4_forest_system.py, same base seed and stream)

cases.selection: as in V1: (sample, row) pairs without a violated bound whose model leakage sum S lies in [0.3, 3]; per (design, point) 8 pairs evenly spread in ln S (indices round(linspace(0, n-1, 8)) of the pairs sorted by ln S, duplicates removed)
cases.feasibility_scan_before_freeze: candidate pairs with S in [0.3, 3] (breast_cancer, split 0, seed 0): P1 t0 123, P1 remap 1 y 112, P1 supply 1 y 61, P3 t0 98, P3 remap 1 y 92, P3 supply 1 y 41 (6T2M for comparison: 880-1628)

netlist.ml: one ML node per case: lumped capacitor C_SA + N C_wire (N = number of features), precharged by .ic to v_pre (no UIC: every other node starts at its DC operating point), released at t = 0; crossing time t_c = first fall of V_ML through v_ref
netlist.lower_bound_LBUF: PCM resistor 1/G from SL_lo to X; divider (nfet_01v8, design W/L, div_lo mismatch of the instance) from X to ground with its gate on the bound's DL source; INV_S 1 (b1n, b1p mismatch) from X to W; INV_S 2 (b2n, b2p mismatch) from W to Z; pull-down (nfet_01v8_lvt 0.42/0.15, pd_lo mismatch) from the ML to ground with its gate on Z
netlist.upper_bound_UINV: as in V1: PCM resistor from SL_hi to Y; divider (div_hi mismatch) from Y to ground; INV_S (un, up mismatch) from Y to Z; pull-down (pd_hi mismatch) with its gate on Z
netlist.unconstrained: 2N minus the number of constrained bounds pull-downs with their gate at 0 V (nominal device), as in V1
netlist.supplies: SL_lo = V_X*,nom + D_eff and SL_hi = V_Y*,nom + D_eff, with D_eff = D (t0, input remap) or D / a_hat (supply node); one data-line source per constrained bound at the voltage of the current input map for the sample's feature value
netlist.conductances: the PCM conductance of each bound after programming noise, drift and read noise, divided as the node prescribes (unchanged for both nodes here), from the E4 machinery
netlist.simulation: ngspice-42, transient as V1 (ml_transient.tran_card, maximum step 0.2 ns), t_stop = 6 t_s(N), 12 cases per netlist, one ngspice process at a time

prediction: t_c,pred = t_s(N) (1 + (2N - 1) w0) / S, with t_s(N) the crossing time of one nominal pull-down at V_sw,nom and all other gates at 0 V, and w0 the leakage of the nominal pull-down at gate 0 V (as V1)

decision.V1GS: pass if |ln(t_c,sim / t_c,pred)| <= 0.05 for at least 90 % of the 48 cases
reported_without_gate: largest |ln(t_c,sim / t_c,pred)|, by design and point
row decisions: model (S >= 1 + (2N - 1) w0) versus simulation (t_c,sim <= t_s); disagreements and those with |ln S| < 0.05
share of S from the lower (LBUF) and the upper (UINV) bounds of each case
gate voltage of every constrained pull-down 2 ns after release, model versus simulation
decision.if_fail: reported as is; the row model and the E4 results are not changed; the paper then states that the gs rows were not validated within the V1 tolerance and gives the measured deviation

smoke.purpose: code check only (netlist builds, ngspice runs, measures parse); its numbers are not used

outputs: results/E4_1_<stamp>/: run_info.json, config_used.json, run.log, cases.json, rows.csv, bounds.csv, checks.json, decision.json
